originality.rationale: The survey at arXiv:2610.22248v1 asks Question 48 without settling normalized positive permutation dynamics. The 2026 expander paper treats linear evolution and plenary identities but does not state the complete limit/support/stability theorem. Jamilov 2210.05107v2 treats a polynomial QSO with a cross-term and a distinguished coordinate, not this projective rational squaring map. Rozikov--Velasco 1803.01503v1 analyzes a distinct mosquito model. Searches of published mathematical records for equivalent normalized permutation-squaring dynamics did not surface a dominating statement; closest items concern different linear/functional/differential systems. Known finite-field algebraic-squaring and automorphism results concern a different domain from nonnegative normalized real orbits. A general projective monomial dynamics source may still cover it and is acknowledged as a residual risk.
residual_risks: The projectivized coordinatewise power map is a familiar elementary dynamical object; a general algebraic-dynamics paper, monomial dynamics work or textbook may contain this theorem under different terminology.
Source inspections focused on relevant full-text sections rather than certifying the absence of an equivalent statement in every work or unpublished source.
The numerical necklace count alone is a known Burnside application, not a claim of independent novelty.

value.rationale: The 2026 evolution-algebra survey Question 48 explicitly asks for graph conditions governing normalized squaring convergence and stability. The result solves all requested features for the entire natural class of positive weighted permutation digraphs, giving explicit topological conjugacy, every omega-limit and basin, superexponential rates, exact stability, complete period distribution and an n-cycle necklace law.
